pure-announcement.rationale: This is the OpenTelemetry project's own launch PR for OBI's first alpha ('we are thrilled to announce'), organized around the release milestone, getting-started links, SIG calls and acknowledgments rather than a technique independent of the product.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (protocol deprecation policy, proxy-boundary capture, MCP notes, OSV, evals) covers eBPF-based zero-code instrumentation.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Claims are checkable against the linked OBI repository, docs and integration tests, and the distributed-tracing limitations are documented at a cited page.

durability.rationale: The protocol-level vs library-level instrumentation trade-off ages well, but the note is anchored to alpha status, a current protocol support list, and per-language tracing gaps that will shift within months.

actionability.rationale: The when-to-use guidance (drop OBI on uninstrumented services, keep SDKs where they work) is real but consists of adoption steps for this one product at its current capability level.

atomicity.rationale: One core idea (eBPF trades universal zero-effort coverage for depth) is stateable in a paragraph, but the note bundles it with release news, marketing claims and getting-started pointers.
